subject: Transportation Systems
title: Braking at 200 mph
description: A micro-lesson that makes Braking at 200 mph usable.

hook.text: A train going 200 mph needs about two miles to stop safely. That's a lot of distance to get wrong.

buildup.text: High-speed trains use a mix of regenerative braking, eddy-current brakes, and disc brakes.

discovery.text: Regenerative braking converts motion back into electricity, feeding power to the overhead wire.

twist.text: Eddy-current brakes use magnets to slow the train without touching the rail at all—no friction, no wear.

climax.text: Emergency braking activates all systems at once. The deceleration is smooth—passengers barely feel it.

punchline.text: Stopping well at 200 mph is harder than going fast.
